userStories.title: Batch Fire-and-Forget DB Inserts in Intent Classifier
userStories.description: 10 separate sequential DB inserts per message. Batch with Promise.allSettled() to reduce pool pressure.
acceptanceCriteria: All fire-and-forget inserts batched

_phaseI.diagnosisBlock:
## Current State

The intent-classifier.ts file contains 9 fire-and-forget DB operations scattered throughout the function, each with `.catch()` handlers:

1. Line 248: `db.insert(rainbowLowconfMessages)` 
2. Line 259: `db.insert(hardCaseQueue)`
3. Line 270: `db.insert(intentAnalytics)`
4. Line 278: `recordIntentLatency()`
5. Line 283: `recordTurnConfidence()`
6. Line 287: `logClassificationDecision()`
7. Line 296: `trackIntentPrediction()`
8. Line 315: `db.insert(escalationQueue)`
9. Line 342: `recordUtteranceGap()`

These are currently fired independently with no coordination, causing them to stress the DB pool sequentially.

## Problem Identified

Each fire-and-forget operation is independent, putting separate load on the PostgreSQL connection pool. When multiple messages arrive in quick succession, the pool gets exhausted. By batching with `Promise.allSettled()`, all operations can start concurrently, reducing peak pool pressure and improving overall throughput.

## Planned Changes

1. Create a `batchFireAndForgetInserts()` function that collects all DB operations into an array
2. Replace individual `.catch()` handlers with structured error logging inside the batch function
3. Call `Promise.allSettled()` on the batch to run all operations concurrently
4. Add test to verify batch execution
